messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - routing anomaly detected for policy `economy-first`. Since 12:43 UTC we see ~35% of traffic routed to variant `gpt-small-quant` (cheap variant). Production quality metric (eval-quality) spiked from 0.7% -> 4.8%. Auto-escalating to on-call and SRE. Ops runbook: https://redwood.ops/runbooks/routing-economy

oncall_meg: taking this — oncall Meg (me) stepping in. Paging SRE and ML-Ops: @sre_ana @ml_ops_jay please ack.

sre_ana: ack, looking now. can you paste the query sample set that shows regressions?

ml_ops_jay: ack. quick data: shadow-eval shows precision drop on completion tasks, and higher hallucination deltas. suspect routing policy reward function prioritized cost too aggressively after recent policy tweak.

oncall_meg: current impact: approx 2.1% of client requests show degraded output quality (based on smoke eval), but because traffic to cheap variant is relatively high in certain routes, 3 enterprise customers (retail-3, travelx, smsify) reported noisy outputs. Support ticket numbers: #3245 #3249 #3251.

support_ravi: support confirms 3 customers opened tickets, one raised immediate escalation to account manager. No major data exfiltration or latency issues reported, only quality.

deploy-bot: NOTE: routing policy `economy-first` updated at 12:40 UTC (deploy id: dep-2024-06-22-401). Change: increased weight for `gpt-small-quant` in low-cost buckets.

ml_ops_jay: if we can, disable the policy or force a fallback to `default-medium` — that will restore quality quickly. Proposed mitigation: (1) disable `economy-first` routing (2) pin critical customers to `default-medium` for 1h (3) run regression eval on the cheap variant.

oncall_meg: executing disable now. command: ```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/routing/policies/economy-first/disable" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"reason":"auto-pager - quality regression"}'
```

oncall_meg: response: {"status":"ok","policy":"economy-first","state":"disabled"} — traffic should start shifting within 30s.

sre_ana: seeing traffic shift in the router logs. Judges (quality counters) trending back to baseline. Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/g/abcd1234/routing-quality (metric: eval-quality).

oncall_meg: running targeted rollback for customers: ```
POST /api/v1/customers/retail-3/routing
{ "variant": "default-medium", "ttl": 3600 }
```

support_ravi: retail-3 confirmed improved outputs after change. ticket #3245 updated — customer says their test examples are back to expected.

pm_leah: thanks. do we need to post to status page? looks like this impacted multiple paying customers.

oncall_meg: I recommend a brief status page entry and an incident notification to the affected customers. status-bot, please create a draft.

status-bot: Draft status page created: https://status.redwood/incident/1729876543 - summary: Temporary routing policy misconfiguration sent disproportionate traffic to a low-cost model variant causing quality regressions for a subset of requests. We disabled the policy and pinned affected customers.

ml_ops_jay: initial hypothesis: policy change increased `cost_weight` parameter from 0.4 -> 0.9 in the scoring function; combined with estimated latency headroom, the router over-selected `gpt-small-quant`. Need to add guardrail that checks eval-quality delta before increasing weight >0.5.

sre_ana: action items (for post-incident): 1) revert policy rollout process to require canary eval on production shadow traffic; 2) add automated rollback if eval-quality delta > 1.0% over baseline; 3) add alert for policy weight jumps above threshold.

oncall_meg: any remaining customer impact?

support_ravi: all three tickets moved to monitoring; customers on the small subset report recovery. No new tickets in last 20m.

pm_leah: do we have a list of other customers in the same segment who might have been silently impacted? we should proactively check.

ml_ops_jay: running an ad-hoc query to list customers with >20% traffic routed to `gpt-small-quant` between 12:40-12:58. I will paste results in 10m.

oncall_meg: handing off to @sre_ana for postmortem and follow-up. I will remain available for questions. Summary for handoff: root cause is routing policy tweak deployed at 12:40 that increased cheap-variant weight without sufficient production eval gates. Immediate mitigation executed: disabled policy, pinned affected customers to default-medium, confirmed quality metrics trending back.

sre_ana: ack, taking over for postmortem. I'll consolidate logs, deploy diff, and timeline. Please assign action items in the postmortem doc.

ml_ops_jay: paste of quick logs (sanitized): ```
[12:39:58] policy-eval: score(gpt-small-quant)=0.87, score(default-medium)=0.45
[12:40:03] router: selected gpt-small-quant for 34% of low-cost requests
[12:45:12] eval-quality: delta +4.1% vs baseline
[12:56:30] policy-disabled by oncall_meg
```

oncall_meg: closing pager. please escalate in the postmortem if we find more affected customers. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 13:02 UTC. Final status: policy disabled, customers pinned, follow-up assigned to SRE/ML-Ops for postmortem and guardrails.

sre_ana: I'll create the postmortem and include planned guardrails + timeline. Assigning owners: ml_ops_jay -> tighten policy evals; pm_leah -> customer comms; support_ravi -> customer outreach; oncall_meg -> verify rollback runbook.

pm_leah: thanks everyone. We'll prepare customer-friendly notes and coordinate with account teams.

support_ravi: monitoring for 2 hours, will reopen ticket if regressions return.

sre_ana: recorded timeline and will ping for review when draft ready.

oncall_meg: thanks team. off-call now.
